clue.text: Sadly disheartened George Orwell, for one

parts.note: George Orwell was the pen name of Eric Blair, an example of an alias

explanation.surface: A sad comment on a downcast George Orwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are expressions of regret or sorrow, interchangeable as an exclamation of grief.

clue.text: Bonding by sharing tiny things: love can flourish over time

indicators.note: in a down clue the anagram sits over, that is above, the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A romantic reading: love that grows over the years creates a bond through little shared things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flourish' rearranges LOVE CAN into COVALEN, which sits 'over' T in this down entry. The tiny things shared are electrons.
explanation.definitionFit: A covalent bond is a chemical link in which two atoms share a pair of electrons.

clue.text: Hairy chap partaking of the sauce

indicators.note: taking a share of the words that follow, so the letters sit within them

explanation.surface: A shaggy fellow helping himself to the gravy.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Jacob's twin brother is described as a hairy man, unlike smooth-skinned Jacob.

clue.text: Irregular forces abruptly quash many a 25's response to Peterloo

explanation.surface: Irregular troops suddenly crush a crowd, which was the Peterloo story itself.

explanation.definitionFit: Shelley wrote this political poem in 1819 as his protest at the killing of demonstrators at St Peter's Field.

clue.text: Stirring at last: 'Shake your chains to earth' like champions!

taking the final letter of each of the quoted words

explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' takes E, R, S, O, H, E from the ends of the six words, and 'Stirring' rearranges them. The quoted line is from the poem at 4 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Champions and the answer are both people celebrated for brave or winning deeds.

clue.text: House of Lords is backing contents of your letter in outline

clue.text: Change of direction regarding Britain in EU capital

clue.text: Weaver caught in Peterloo massacre

indicators.note: trapped within the words that follow, so the letters lie inside them

explanation.surface: A textile worker was trapped in the Peterloo killings, as many Manchester weavers were.
explanation.definitionFit: A loom is the machine that weaves thread into cloth, so it is a weaver in a mechanical sense.

clue.text: Pride perhaps lacking in many soldiers

clue.text: On camera, I ground coffee

the existing state of affairs, which conservatives wish to keep

clue.text: Austerity of centrists distorted society

clue.text: Run to join forces and gain strength

people come together for a common cause
to recover, as prices or a patient do

explanation.walkthrough: This clue gives three separate definitions in a row, joined by 'to' and 'and'.

clue.text: Subsequently cut both ends off beams

clue.text: Fens used to be drained, Hull also
